Badge.reason: matBadge is Material's small labelled/numeric indicator directive. React's Badge renders the same small labelled shape -- an optional dot plus text, no interactive affordance of its own -- and Arena has no arena-badge primitive and should not grow one. arena-material.css does not dress it: no .mat-badge-content rule exists in the bridge today, so its colours are Material's own defaults, not Arena's tokens.

Calendar.reason: This entry and CalendarEvent below are the only two in this file that are genuinely absent rather than delegated -- pattern "absent", not "none", because Angular has no such component at all, not a rendered-but-inert one. Arena's Calendar is a day/hour schedule grid with absolutely-positioned event blocks -- a scheduling view, not a date picker. Angular Material's calendar surface (mat-calendar, the view inside MatDatepicker) is a month/date-selection grid: a different widget solving a different problem, with no day/hour axis and no event blocks. There is no real Material control this delegates to, and arena-material.css dresses none. Whether Angular should gain a schedule view is a separate, open question this entry does not answer: it records that React has one and Angular does not, not a decision that Angular never will. Nothing has decided either way. Recorded in CLAUDE.md's Known debt.

CalendarEvent.reason: Absent for the same reason Calendar is, one level down: a CalendarEvent is a chip inside Arena's schedule grid, and Angular has no schedule grid for one to live in. It is not delegated -- Material has no per-event chip because it has no day/hour view, and arena-material.css dresses none. This entry exists because CalendarEvent became a React component in plan 8C3 (it had been a predefined object in api/types/), and every React component declares for every layer. It records the same open question Calendar's entry does and answers it no further: if Angular ever gains a schedule view, this is the second component that decision creates.

Card.reason: MatCard already provides the bordered surface and its header/content/actions slots; it manages no interactive state of its own, the same as React's Card. The bridge dresses its container colour (--surface-card) and --r-lg radius. Arena has no arena-card primitive and should not grow one.

Dialog.reason: MatDialog (the CDK dialog underneath it) provides the modal surface, aria-modal, first-focus-on-open, restore-focus-on-close and Escape-to-close -- the entire requirement list React's own Dialog binding records as unmet. The bridge dresses the surface colour and --r-lg radius on .mat-mdc-dialog-surface. Arena has no arena-dialog primitive and should not grow one.

Menu.reason: The matMenuTriggerFor directive sets aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the actual focusable trigger element (not a wrapping node, which is exactly where React's own Menu binding records this as unmet), moves focus to the first item on open, and the CDK overlay under it implements Escape and arrow-key navigation inside the panel. arena-material.css has no rule for the menu panel or its items, so it renders in Material's own colours, not Arena's tokens, today.

Pagination.reason: MatPaginator already renders a labelled control set for moving between pages of a data set. arena-material.css does not dress it -- no .mat-mdc-paginator rule exists in the bridge today -- so its colours are Material's own defaults, not Arena's tokens.

cases.name: determinate
cases.when: mode is determinate or buffer -- MatProgressBar reports a value and sets aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax from it

exceptions.reason: MatProgressBar sets no aria-live at all, and role="progressbar" carries no implicit politeness the way role="status" does, so a screen reader is not guaranteed to announce value changes. Arena's own React ProgressBar sets aria-live="polite" explicitly; this is where the two layers genuinely differ, and it is a real gap for an Angular user rather than a description problem.

cases.name: indeterminate
cases.when: mode is indeterminate or query -- MatProgressBar reports that work is under way without a value, and the three value attributes are correctly absent

exceptions.reason: The same gap as the determinate case, and declared again because an exception names one requirement in one case: MatProgressBar sets no aria-live in either mode. This is one defect declared twice, not two defects.

ProgressBar.reason: MatProgressBar renders the indicator, its determinate/indeterminate/buffer/query modes and its value plumbing (aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax). The bridge dresses its active-indicator and track colour on the brand and border tokens. Arena has no arena-progress-bar primitive and should not grow one.

exceptions.reason: Angular Material's own accessibility docs state that MatButtonToggleGroup applies role="group", not role="radiogroup" -- this pattern's literal requirement -- to the group element, even in its default single-selection (exclusive) mode. A consumer must still label the group with aria-label or aria-labelledby, which the docs also call out.

SegmentedControl.reason: In its default (non-multiple) mode, MatButtonToggleGroup behaves like a radio-button group: exactly one toggle is selected, its value drives the group's own, and it supports ngModel the way a radio group does. arena-material.css does not dress it -- no .mat-button-toggle-group rule exists in the bridge today -- so its colours are Material's own defaults, not Arena's tokens.

Select.reason: MatSelect follows the ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern directly (Angular Material's own accessibility docs say so in those words): the trigger controls a role="listbox" popup, with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant wired by the component rather than left implicit the way React's native <select> leaves them. Like Input, it is composed inside <mat-form-field appearance="outline">, and the bridge dresses that field, not the select element itself. Arena has no arena-select primitive and should not grow one. `divergesFrom` names `select` because React's Select is the NATIVE element: a <select> whose popup the browser renders and operates, so aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant are the user agent's business and authoring them would be a claim the component cannot keep true. MatSelect is the opposite -- an authored combobox with a real listbox in the overlay -- so the two layers implement genuinely different things under one contract. Neither is wrong, and the difference is not cosmetic: a native select gets the platform's own mobile picker, while MatSelect gets consistent styling and Arena's tokens. Recorded rather than reconciled.

SideNav.reason: mat-nav-list already provides the anchor-or-button distinction, the active state and the keyboard behaviour. The bridge declares colour, weight, font and shape and deliberately no geometry -- re-specifying Material's list metrics is the duplication the bridge exists to avoid. See DOUBTS.md section 3's SideNav entry for the full three-way comparison.

SideNavCollapsible.reason: A consumer needing a collapsible group inside a mat-nav-list reaches for MatExpansionPanel, and it binds the same pattern React's own SideNavCollapsible binds rather than `none`, because the header IS the disclosure button. Every one of the six requirements is met by Material itself, verified against @angular/material 22.0.5's own expansion bundle rather than assumed: mat-expansion-panel-header carries a static role="button" host attribute (it is not a native <button>, which is the pattern's own second clause), an attr.tabindex binding, [attr.aria-expanded] bound to the panel's expanded state and [attr.aria-controls] bound to the panel's id, and its _keydown handler switches on ENTER and SPACE from @angular/cdk/keycodes and toggles the panel. Its accessible name is the projected mat-panel-title text, which the disclosure pattern accepts as text content. NO dressedBy IS CLAIMED, and that is a real gap rather than an omission: arena-material.css has no rule for any .mat-expansion-* host class today, so a panel used in an Arena sidebar renders in Material's own surface, radius and typography instead of Arena's tokens -- the same honesty the SideNavSection and TableCell entries use where the bridge is silent. What Material adds beyond React's binding is an accordion mode (mat-accordion), where a header's other keys are forwarded to _handleHeaderKeydown for arrow navigation between panels; React's collapsibles are independent disclosures with no such mode, which is a capability difference and not a pattern disagreement -- the disclosure pattern requires neither. Nothing here is machine-checked: the Material version above is recorded in this reason string only, which is the gap CLAUDE.md's Known debt records for every delegated entry and this one inherits rather than closes.

SideNavItem.delegatedTo: Angular Material mat-nav-list's own list item (mat-list-item)
SideNavItem.reason: React's SideNav became a compound component so that sections and nested groups are expressible at all, and SideNavItem is the leaf that shape needs; Angular needs no counterpart primitive, because mat-nav-list's list item is the same anchor-or-button leaf and the consumer writes one per destination inside the list exactly as they now write one SideNavItem per destination in React. The pattern is `none` for the same reason React's own binding is: which element an item renders is decided per item, so no single interactive pattern always applies to it, and what the rendered element does carry comes from the platform and from the enclosing list's `navigation` binding -- which the SideNav entry above records and this one does not restate. What the bridge dresses at the ITEM level is checkable by selector rather than asserted in general: `.arena-side-nav.mat-mdc-nav-list` sets the item label's font, size, weight and colour and the active indicator's shape, and `.arena-side-nav .mdc-list-item--activated` sets the active item's indicator colour, label colour and label weight. Nothing here claims what Material version those hosts belong to; that gap is the one CLAUDE.md's Known debt records for every delegated entry, and this entry inherits it rather than closing it.

SideNavSection.delegatedTo: Angular Material mat-nav-list's own <div mat-subheader> grouping
SideNavSection.reason: mat-nav-list groups items with the matSubheader directive applied to a heading element Material renders inside the list; the consumer writes one per group inside the list exactly as they now write one SideNavSection per group in React. It carries no interactive affordance of its own -- every control inside it is the list's own item, matching pattern `none` for the same reason React's own binding is. arena-material.css has no rule for the subheader host class today, so it renders in Material's own colours, not Arena's tokens -- no dressedBy is claimed, the same honesty the TableCell entry uses for its data cells.

exceptions.reason: MatProgressSpinner sets no aria-live, and role="progressbar" carries no implicit politeness the way role="status" does. Arena's own React Spinner sets aria-live="polite" explicitly, so this is where the two layers genuinely differ.

Spinner.reason: MatProgressSpinner renders the indicator and its determinate/indeterminate/buffer/query modes, with aria-valuenow mirrored from value. The bridge dresses its active-indicator colour on the brand. Arena has no arena-spinner primitive and should not grow one.

Tab.reason: React's Tabs became a compound component so that a tabpanel is rendered at all, and Tab is the leaf that shape needs; Angular needs no counterpart primitive, because <mat-tab> is the same leaf -- the consumer writes one per view inside <mat-tab-group> exactly as they now write one Tab per view inside Tabs. The pattern is `none` for the same reason React's own binding is: every requirement that applies to a tab is a clause of the `tabs` pattern, which the enclosing group binds. Verified against @angular/material 22.0.5.

exceptions.reason: MatTable defaults to role="table", not role="grid" (Angular Material's own accessibility docs). The role can be changed by hand, but nothing in Arena's usage does, so this stays unmet the same way React's own Table binding records it.
Row role follows the table's own role -- with the default role="table", rows carry row semantics appropriate to a table, not the grid pattern's roving-focus row, mirroring React's own exception.
Same as roles.row: cell roles follow the default table role, not the grid pattern's gridcell/columnheader/rowheader, mirroring React's own exception.

Material's own docs say to always provide aria-label or aria-labelledby on the table element; nothing in this delegation supplies one, so it is unmet the same way React's own Table binding records it.

Angular Material's own accessibility docs are explicit: switching to role="grid" or role="treegrid" 'does not add keyboard input handling or focus management' -- there is no roving tab stop either way.
Per the same Material docs quote: changing the role adds no keyboard input handling at all, so arrow-key navigation is unmet regardless of which role is set.
Same as ArrowKeys -- Material supplies no keyboard handling of the grid, with either role.
Same as ArrowKeys -- Material supplies no keyboard handling of the grid, with either role.

Table.reason: MatTable provides the row/column definition machinery (matColumnDef, mat-header-row, mat-row) and a real data-bound table, rather than a bespoke Arena re-implementation of table layout. The bridge dresses its background and row hairline colour, and gives the header cell the mono uppercase micro-label treatment. Arena has no arena-table primitive and should not grow one. React's own Table declares TWO cases -- a wide `grid` and, below --bp-md, a `card` shape bound to `none` where no table element is rendered at all. `divergesFrom` names that second one: MatTable has a single shape and no responsive card layout, so there is no render here for it to describe. That is a capability difference rather than a defect, and it leaves this entry measured against `grid` alone, which is what the exceptions below are about.

TableCell.delegatedTo: Angular Material MatTable (mat-cell / matCellDef, mat-header-cell / matHeaderCellDef)
TableCell.reason: React's Table became a compound component to keep a Badge in a status cell and a Button in an actions cell without per-item projection, and TableCell is the leaf that shape needs. Angular needs no counterpart primitive: MatTable already gives the consumer a per-cell template (matCellDef), so the same content is written inline in the column definition and no arena-table-cell would add anything. Like React's own TableCell it carries no interactive affordance of its own -- a control inside a Material cell comes from the consumer's template. The bridge dresses the HEADER cell specifically, with the mono uppercase micro-label treatment (.mat-mdc-header-cell); it adds no rule to a data cell.

TableRow.delegatedTo: Angular Material MatTable (mat-row / matRowDef, mat-header-row / matHeaderRowDef)
TableRow.reason: MatTable's row definitions produce the rows, and every requirement that applies to one is a clause of the `grid` pattern the Table entry above binds -- where Material's shortcomings are already recorded, in eight exceptions covering the row and cell roles, the roving tab stop and the arrow keys. Recording them again here was duplication: five exceptions restating what the Table entry says, on an element that owns none of the behaviour. This mirrors React's own TableRow, whose `row` case binds `none` for exactly that reason, and it is the same shape as Tab under `tabs` and SideNavItem under `navigation`. `divergesFrom` names `button` because React's TableRow declares a case this layer has no counterpart for: below --bp-md React renders each row as a <div>, which CAN carry role="button" and does. MatTable has one shape and no responsive card layout, so there is no render here for that case to describe -- a real capability difference, not a defect in either layer. The row's hairline colour is set from a custom property on the table host (--mat-table-row-item-outline-color on .mat-mdc-table), not by any rule targeting the row, so no dressedBy is claimed for it.

Tabs.reason: MatTabGroup already provides the tablist/tab/tabpanel role triad, aria-selected, roving focus and Left/Right arrow-key navigation between tabs -- the entire list React's own Tabs binding records as unmet. The bridge dresses the active label and indicator colour on the brand. Arena has no arena-tabs primitive and should not grow one.

Toast.reason: MatSnackBar owns the surface, its enter/exit animation and its dismissal (action button, explicit dismiss(), or an optional duration). The bridge dresses the snack-bar container colour, --r-md radius and supporting-text colour. Arena has no arena-toast primitive and should not grow one.
